sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya govindaḥ sādhu sādhv ity athābravīt śaraveśmani pārthena kṛte tasmin mahāraṇe
english: Then Govinda laughed and cried, "Well done! Well done!" when Pārtha had fashioned that house of arrows there in the midst of the great battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca salile janite tasmin kaunteyena mahātmanā nivārite dviṣatsainye kṛte ca śaraveśmani
english: Saṃjaya said: When that water had been brought forth by the great-souled son of Kuntī, when the enemy host had been held off and the house of arrows wrought,

sanskrit: vāsudevo rathāt tūrṇam avatīrya mahādyutiḥ mocayām āsa turagān vitunnān kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Vāsudeva of great splendour swiftly dismounted from the chariot and unyoked the horses, pierced as they were by heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ tad dṛṣṭvā siṃhanādo mahān abhūt siddhacāraṇasaṃghānāṃ sainikānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Beholding that thing never seen before, a mighty lion-roar arose on every side from the hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas and from the soldiers.

sanskrit: padātinaṃ tu kaunteyaṃ yudhyamānaṃ nararṣabhāḥ nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Yet those bulls among men could not hold back the son of Kuntī as he fought on foot — and that was as if a marvel.

sanskrit: āpatatsu rathaugheṣu prabhūtagajavājiṣu nāsaṃbhramat tadā pārthas tad asya puruṣān ati
english: Though floods of chariots came rushing on, thick with elephants and horses, Pārtha was not dismayed — and this surpassed all other men.

sanskrit: vyasṛjanta śaraughāṃs te pāṇḍavaṃ prati pārthivāḥ na cāvyathata dharmātmā vāsaviḥ paravīrahā
english: Those kings loosed floods of arrows against the Pāṇḍava, yet the righteous son of Vāsava, slayer of hostile heroes, did not falter.

sanskrit: sa tāni śarajālāni gadāḥ prāsāṃś ca vīryavān āgatān agrasat pārthaḥ saritaḥ sāgaro yathā
english: Those nets of arrows, those maces and javelins that came upon him, the valiant Pārtha swallowed up as the ocean swallows the rivers.

sanskrit: astravegena mahatā pārtho bāhubalena ca sarveṣāṃ pārthivendrāṇām agrasat tāñ śarottamān
english: With the great speed of his weapons and the strength of his arms, Pārtha swallowed up the finest shafts of all those lords of kings.

sanskrit: tat tu pārthasya vikrāntaṃ vāsudevasya cobhayoḥ apūjayan mahārāja kauravāḥ paramādbhutam
english: That prowess of both Pārtha and Vāsudeva, O great king, the Kauravas extolled as utterly wondrous.

sanskrit: kim adbhutataraṃ loke bhavitāpy atha vāpy abhūt yad aśvān pārthagovindau mocayām āsatū raṇe
english: What greater marvel has ever been in the world, or shall ever be, than that Pārtha and Govinda should unyoke their horses in the very midst of battle?

sanskrit: bhayaṃ vipulam asmāsu tāv adhattāṃ narottamau tejo vidadhatuś cograṃ visrabdhau raṇamūrdhani
english: Those two best of men struck vast fear into us and displayed their fierce energy, wholly unconcerned at the very front of the fray.

sanskrit: athotsmayan hṛṣīkeśaḥ strīmadhya iva bhārata arjunena kṛte saṃkhye śaragarbhagṛhe tadā
english: Then Hṛṣīkeśa, smiling, as though amid women, O Bhārata, when Arjuna had made that inner chamber of arrows on the field,

sanskrit: upāvartayad avyagras tān aśvān puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ miṣatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ tvadīyānāṃ viśāṃ pate
english: The lotus-eyed one, untroubled, led those horses round, before the very eyes of all your hosts, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śramaṃ ca glāniṃ ca vepathuṃ vamathuṃ vraṇān sarvaṃ vyapānudat kṛṣṇaḥ kuśalo hy aśvakarmaṇi
english: Their fatigue and faintness, their trembling, their retching, their wounds — all of it Kṛṣṇa drove away, skilled as he was in the handling of horses.

sanskrit: śalyān uddhṛtya pāṇibhyāṃ parimṛjya ca tān hayān upāvṛtya yathānyāyaṃ pāyayām āsa vāri saḥ
english: Drawing out the barbs with his hands and rubbing down those horses, he turned them about in due order and gave them the water to drink.

sanskrit: sa tāṃl labdhodakān snātāñ jagdhānnān vigataklamān yojayām āsa saṃhṛṣṭaḥ punar eva rathottame
english: Then, well pleased, he yoked them once more to that finest of chariots — watered, washed, fed, and freed of weariness.

sanskrit: sa taṃ rathavaraṃ śauriḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ samāsthāya mahātejāḥ sārjunaḥ prayayau drutam
english: Then Śauri of great splendour, foremost of all who bear arms, mounted that excellent chariot together with Arjuna and swiftly drove on.

sanskrit: rathaṃ rathavarasyājau yuktaṃ labdhodakair hayaiḥ dṛṣṭvā kurubalaśreṣṭhāḥ punar vimanaso 'bhavan
english: Seeing the chariot of that best of warriors yoked with horses now watered, the foremost of the Kuru host grew downcast once again.

sanskrit: viniḥśvasantas te rājan bhagnadaṃṣṭrā ivoragāḥ dhig aho dhig gataḥ pārthaḥ kṛṣṇaś cety abruvan pṛthak
english: Hissing, O king, like serpents whose fangs are broken, they each cried out, "Shame, oh shame! Pārtha and Kṛṣṇa have slipped away!"

sanskrit: sarvakṣatrasya miṣato rathenaikena daṃśitau bālakrīḍanakeneva kadarthīkṛtya no balam
english: Before the eyes of all the warriors, those two mailed in armour, with a single chariot, made our might contemptible, as though it were a child's plaything.

sanskrit: krośatāṃ yatamānānām asaṃsaktau paraṃtapau darśayitvātmano vīryaṃ prayātau sarvarājasu
english: While we cried out and strove against them, those two scorchers of foes, untouched, displayed their valour and passed on through all the kings.

sanskrit: tau prayātau punar dṛṣṭvā tadānye sainikābruvan tvaradhvaṃ kuravaḥ sarve vadhe kṛṣṇakirīṭinoḥ
english: Seeing the two pressing on again, other soldiers then cried, "Make haste, all you Kurus, to slay Kṛṣṇa and the Diademed One!"

sanskrit: rathaṃ yuktvā hi dāśārho miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām jayadrathāya yāty eṣa kadarthīkṛtya no raṇe
english: "For the Dāśārha, having yoked the chariot before the eyes of all the bowmen, drives on toward Jayadratha, making mock of us in battle!"

sanskrit: tatra ke cin mitho rājan samabhāṣanta bhūmipāḥ adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ saṃgrāme tad dṛṣṭvā mahad adbhutam
english: There some of the kings spoke among themselves, O king, beholding in that battle that great marvel never seen before:

sanskrit: sarvasainyāni rājā ca dhṛtarāṣṭro 'tyayaṃ gataḥ duryodhanāparādhena kṣatraṃ kṛtsnā ca medinī
english: "All these hosts, and King Dhṛtarāṣṭra too, are come to ruin; through Duryodhana's offence the whole warrior race and the entire earth,

sanskrit: vilayaṃ samanuprāptā tac ca rājā na budhyate ity evaṃ kṣatriyās tatra bruvanty anye ca bhārata
english: "have come to dissolution, and yet the king does not perceive it." Thus did the warriors there speak, and others too, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sindhurājasya yat kṛtyaṃ gatasya yamasādanam tat karotu vṛthādṛṣṭir dhārtarāṣṭro 'nupāyavit
english: "Whatever rites are due for the king of the Sindhus, now gone to Yama's abode, let Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son perform — he of vain vision, ignorant of the means."

sanskrit: tataḥ śīghrataraṃ prāyāt pāṇḍavaḥ saindhavaṃ prati nivartamāne tigmāṃśau hṛṣṭaiḥ pītodakair hayaiḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍava drove faster still toward the Saindhava, as the fierce-rayed sun was sinking, with horses now glad and watered.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ mahābāhuṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ yodhāḥ kruddham ivāntakam
english: The warriors could not hold back that mighty-armed one, foremost of all who bear arms, as he drove on like Death enraged.

sanskrit: vidrāvya tu tataḥ sainyaṃ pāṇḍavaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ yathā mṛgagaṇān siṃhaḥ saindhavārthe vyaloḍayat
english: Then the Pāṇḍava, tormentor of foes, having scattered the host, churned it up for the Saindhava's sake as a lion churns a herd of deer.

sanskrit: gāhamānas tv anīkāni tūrṇam aśvān acodayat balākavarṇān dāśārhaḥ pāñcajanyaṃ vyanādayat
english: Plunging into the ranks, the Dāśārha swiftly urged on the crane-coloured horses and made Pāñcajanya resound.

sanskrit: kaunteyenāgrataḥ sṛṣṭā nyapatan pṛṣṭhataḥ śarāḥ tūrṇāt tūrṇataraṃ hy aśvās te 'vahan vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: The arrows loosed in front by the son of Kuntī fell behind him, so swiftly — faster than fast — did those wind-swift horses bear him on.

sanskrit: vātoddhūtapatākāntaṃ rathaṃ jaladanisvanam ghoraṃ kapidhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣaṇṇā rathino 'bhavan
english: Beholding that terrible ape-bannered chariot, its pennon tossing in the wind, rumbling like a thundercloud, the chariot-warriors fell into despair.

sanskrit: divākare 'tha rajasā sarvataḥ saṃvṛte bhṛśam śarārtāś ca raṇe yodhā na kṛṣṇau śekur īkṣitum
english: And as the sun was thickly veiled on every side by dust, the warriors, sore beset by arrows, could not even look upon the two Kṛṣṇas in the fight.

sanskrit: tato nṛpatayaḥ kruddhāḥ parivavrur dhanaṃjayam kṣatriyā bahavaś cānye jayadrathavadhaiṣiṇam
english: Then the kings, enraged, encircled Dhanaṃjaya, and many other warriors as well, as he sought the slaying of Jayadratha.

sanskrit: apanīyatsu śalyeṣu dhiṣṭhitaṃ puruṣarṣabham duryodhanas tv agāt pārthaṃ tvaramāṇo mahāhave
english: While the barbs were being drawn out, Duryodhana came hastening against Pārtha, that steadfast bull among men, in the great battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sraṃsanta iva majjānas tāvakānāṃ bhayān nṛpa tau dṛṣṭvā samatikrāntau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Saṃjaya said: The very marrow of your men seemed to melt with fear, O king, when they saw Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya break clean through.

sanskrit: sarve tu pratisaṃrabdhā hrīmantaḥ sattvacoditāḥ sthirībūtā mahātmānaḥ pratyagacchan dhanaṃjayam
english: Yet all the great-souled ones, stung to wrath, full of shame, urged on by their own courage, stood firm and went forth again to meet Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: ye gatāḥ pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe krodhāmarṣasamanvitāḥ te 'dyāpi na nivartante sindhavaḥ sāgarād iva
english: Those who went against the Pāṇḍava in the fight, filled with wrath and indignation — even now they do not turn back, as rivers do not turn back from the sea.

sanskrit: asantas tu nyavartanta vedebhya iva nāstikāḥ narakaṃ bhajamānās te pratyapadyanta kilbiṣam
english: But the base ones turned away, as unbelievers turn from the Vedas, and, partaking of hell, they came into sin.

sanskrit: tāv atītya rathānīkaṃ vimuktau puruṣarṣabhau dadṛśāte yathā rāhor āsyān muktau prabhākarau
english: Those two bulls among men, having passed beyond the chariot-array and broken free, appeared like two suns escaped from the maw of Rāhu.

sanskrit: matsyāv iva mahājālaṃ vidārya vigatajvarau tathā kṛṣṇāv adṛśyetāṃ senājālaṃ vidārya tat
english: As two fishes that have rent a great net are freed of their distress, so did the two Kṛṣṇas appear, having torn through that net of the army.

sanskrit: vimuktau śastrasaṃbādhād droṇānīkāt sudurbhidāt adṛśyetāṃ mahātmānau kālasūryāv ivoditau
english: Set free from the press of weapons, from Droṇa's array so hard to pierce, those two great-souled ones appeared like two risen suns of the Doom-time.

sanskrit: astrasaṃbādhanirmuktau vimuktau śastrasaṃkaṭāt adṛśyetāṃ mahātmānau śatrusaṃbādhakāriṇau
english: Released from the crush of missiles, freed from the throng of weapons, those two great-souled ones appeared, dealers of distress to their foes.

sanskrit: vimuktau jvalanasparśān makarāsyāj jhaṣāv iva vyakṣobhayetāṃ senāṃ tau samudraṃ makarāv iva
english: Freed from a touch like fire, as two fishes from the jaws of a crocodile, the two convulsed the host as a pair of sea-monsters convulse the ocean.

sanskrit: tāvakās tava putrāś ca droṇānīkasthayos tayoḥ naitau tariṣyato droṇam iti cakrus tadā matim
english: Your men and your sons, while those two were still within Droṇa's array, resolved in their minds: "These two shall not pass beyond Droṇa."

sanskrit: tau tu dṛṣṭvā vyatikrāntau droṇānīkaṃ mahādyutī nāśaśaṃsur mahārāja sindhurājasya jīvitam
english: But when they saw those two of great splendour break past Droṇa's array, O great king, they no longer hoped for the life of the king of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: āśā balavatī rājan putrāṇām abhavat tava droṇahārdikyayoḥ kṛṣṇau na mokṣyete iti prabho
english: A strong hope had been your sons', O king: "From Droṇa and the son of Hṛdika the two Kṛṣṇas shall not escape," O lord.

sanskrit: tām āśāṃ viphalāṃ kṛtvā nistīrṇau tau paraṃtapau droṇānīkaṃ mahārāja bhojānīkaṃ ca dustaram
english: Making that hope fruitless, those two scorchers of foes crossed beyond Droṇa's array, O great king, and the Bhoja array so hard to pass.

sanskrit: atha dṛṣṭvā vyatikrāntau jvalitāv iva pāvakau nirāśāḥ sindhurājasya jīvitaṃ nāśaśaṃsire
english: Then, seeing the two pass through like blazing fires, they grew hopeless and no longer looked for the life of the king of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: mithaś ca samabhāṣetām abhītau bhayavardhanau jayadrathavadhe vācas tās tāḥ kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau
english: And the two — Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya, fearless and striking fear into others — spoke together such words as these concerning the slaying of Jayadratha:

sanskrit: asau madhye kṛtaḥ ṣaḍbhir dhārtarāṣṭrair mahārathaiḥ cakṣurviṣayasaṃprāpto na nau mokṣyati saindhavaḥ
english: "Yonder Saindhava, set in the midst by six great car-warriors, sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, has come within range of our sight; he shall not escape us."

sanskrit: yady asya samare goptā śakro devagaṇaiḥ saha tathāpy enaṃ haniṣyāva iti kṛṣṇāv abhāṣatām
english: "Even though Śakra with the hosts of gods should guard him in the battle, even so we shall slay him" — thus spoke the two Kṛṣṇas.

sanskrit: iti kṛṣṇau mahābāhū mithaḥ kathayatāṃ tadā sindhurājam avekṣantau tat putrās tava śuśruvuḥ
english: As the two mighty-armed Kṛṣṇas spoke thus to each other, gazing upon the king of the Sindhus, your sons overheard them.

sanskrit: atītya marudhanveva prayāntau tṛṣitau gajau pītvā vāri samāśvastau tathaivāstām ariṃdamau
english: Like two thirsting elephants who, having crossed a desert waste, drink water and are refreshed and pass on, so stood those two subduers of foes.

sanskrit: vyāghrasiṃhagajākīrṇān atikramyeva parvatān adṛśyetāṃ mahābāhū yathā mṛtyujarātigau
english: Like men who have crossed mountains thronged with tigers, lions, and elephants, the two mighty-armed ones appeared, as though gone beyond death and old age.

sanskrit: tathā hi mukhavarṇo 'yam anayor iti menire tāvakā dṛśya muktau tau vikrośanti sma sarvataḥ
english: "Such indeed is the look upon the faces of these two," so thought your men, and seeing them broken free, they cried out on every side.

sanskrit: droṇād āśīviṣākārāj jvalitād iva pāvakāt anyebhyaḥ pārthivebhyaś ca bhāsvantāv iva bhāskarau
english: From Droṇa, shaped like a venomous serpent, like a blazing fire, and from the other kings, the two shone forth radiant as twin suns.

sanskrit: tau muktau sāgaraprakhyād droṇānīkād ariṃdamau adṛśyetāṃ mudā yuktau samuttīryārṇavaṃ yathā
english: Those two subduers of foes, freed from Droṇa's array that was like an ocean, appeared filled with joy, as men who have crossed over the sea.

sanskrit: śastraughān mahato muktau droṇahārdikyarakṣitān rocamānāv adṛśyetām indrāgnyoḥ sadṛśau raṇe
english: Freed from the vast floods of weapons guarded by Droṇa and the son of Hṛdika, the two appeared resplendent in the fight, the equals of Indra and Agni.

sanskrit: udbhinnarudhirau kṛṣṇau bhāradvājasya sāyakaiḥ śitaiś citau vyarocetāṃ karṇikārair ivācalau
english: Their blood welling forth, the two Kṛṣṇas, studded with the sharp shafts of Bhāradvāja, shone like two mountains decked with karṇikāra blossoms.

sanskrit: droṇagrāhahradān muktau śaktyāśīviṣasaṃkaṭāt ayaḥśarogramakarāt kṣatriyapravarāmbhasaḥ
english: Released from the lake whose crocodile was Droṇa, beset with the venomous serpents of its spears, with iron arrows for its fierce sea-monsters, with the foremost warriors for its waters —

sanskrit: jyāghoṣatalanirhrādād gadānistriṃśavidyutaḥ droṇāstrameghān nirmuktau sūryendū timirād iva
english: — with the twang of bowstrings and the slap of palms for its roar, with maces and swords for its lightning: from that cloud of Droṇa's weapons the two broke free, like sun and moon from the dark.

sanskrit: bāhubhyām iva saṃtīrṇau sindhuṣaṣṭhāḥ samudragāḥ tapānte saritaḥ pūrṇā mahāgrāhasamākulāḥ
english: As though they had crossed by their own arms the brimming rivers that run to the sea, the Sindhu sixth among them, swollen at summer's end and teeming with great monsters —

sanskrit: iti kṛṣṇau maheṣvāsau yaśasā lokaviśrutau sarvabhūtāny amanyanta droṇāstrabalavismayāt
english: — so did all beings deem the two Kṛṣṇas, those great archers renowned throughout the worlds for their glory, in their wonder at the might of Droṇa's weapons.

sanskrit: jayadrathaṃ samīpastham avekṣantau jighāṃsayā ruruṃ nipāne lipsantau vyāghravat tāv atiṣṭhatām
english: Gazing with longing to slay upon Jayadratha, who stood close by, the two waited like tigers eager to take a ruru-deer at the watering place.

sanskrit: yathā hi mukhavarṇo 'yam anayor iti menire tava yodhā mahārāja hatam eva jayadratham
english: "Such indeed is the look upon the faces of these two," thought your warriors, O great king, and they counted Jayadratha already slain.

sanskrit: lohitākṣau mahābāhū saṃyattau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau sindhurājam abhiprekṣya hṛṣṭau vyanadatāṃ muhuḥ
english: Red-eyed and mighty-armed, intent upon their purpose, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava, gazing upon the king of the Sindhus, roared again and again in their gladness.

sanskrit: śaurer abhīśuhastasya pārthasya ca dhanuṣmataḥ tayor āsīt pratibhrājaḥ sūryapāvakayor iva
english: From Śauri with the reins in his hands and from Pārtha bearing his bow there came a radiance as of the sun and fire.

sanskrit: harṣa eva tayor āsīd droṇānīkapramuktayoḥ samīpe saindhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā śyenayor āmiṣaṃ yathā
english: Joy alone was theirs, freed now from Droṇa's array, as they saw the Saindhava close at hand, as two hawks behold their prey.

sanskrit: tau tu saindhavam ālokya vartamānam ivāntike sahasā petatuḥ kruddhau kṣipraṃ śyenāv ivāmiṣe
english: Beholding the Saindhava as though within their very reach, the two, enraged, swooped down at once and swiftly, like two hawks upon their prey.

sanskrit: tau tu dṛṣṭvā vyatikrāntau hṛṣīkeśadhanaṃjayau sindhurājasya rakṣārthaṃ parākrāntaḥ sutas tava
english: But seeing Hṛṣīkeśa and Dhanaṃjaya break through, your son strode forth in valour to guard the king of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: droṇenābaddhakavaco rājā duryodhanas tadā yayāv ekarathenājau hayasaṃskāravit prabho
english: His armour fastened on by Droṇa, King Duryodhana, knowing well the management of horses, then drove into the battle with a single chariot, O lord.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇapārthau maheṣvāsau vyatikramyātha te sutaḥ agrataḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ pratīyāya narādhipa
english: Passing the great archers Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha, your son then went forth to confront the lotus-eyed one face to face, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarveṣu sainyeṣu vāditrāṇi prahṛṣṭavat prāvādyan samatikrānte tava putre dhanaṃjayam
english: Then throughout all the hosts the instruments sounded out joyfully when your son had passed beyond Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: siṃhanādaravāś cāsañ śaṅkhadundubhimiśritāḥ dṛṣṭvā duryodhanaṃ tatra kṛṣṇayoḥ pramukhe sthitam
english: And lion-roars arose, mingled with the blare of conches and drums, as they saw Duryodhana standing there before the two Kṛṣṇas.

sanskrit: ye ca te sindhurājasya goptāraḥ pāvakopamāḥ te prahṛṣyanta samare dṛṣṭvā putraṃ tavābhibho
english: And those who were the guardians of the king of the Sindhus, like flames of fire, rejoiced in the battle to behold your son, O lord.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā duryodhanaṃ kṛṣṇas tv atikrāntaṃ sahānugam abravīd arjunaṃ rājan prāptakālam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: But seeing Duryodhana come forth with his followers, Kṛṣṇa spoke to Arjuna, O king, these words befitting the hour:

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca suyodhanam atikrāntam enaṃ paśya dhanaṃjaya āpadgatam imaṃ manye nāsty asya sadṛśo rathaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Behold this Suyodhana come forth before us, Dhanaṃjaya; fallen into peril, I deem him — there is no chariot-warrior the equal of his.
